result.topic_en: Euler begins the solution of a maximum problem for a space curve. The integral is ∫w s dx, with w a function of the radius v and s = √(1+p²+q²). He computes the differential coefficients M, N, N', P, P' and S. From these he derives three Euler-type equations and reduces them to two differential equations.
result.transcription:
34
Solutio.
31. Facto igitur $\partial y = p\partial x$ et $\partial z = q\partial x$, positoque $\sqrt{(1+pp+qq)} = s$, erit formula nostra Maximi $\int ws\,\partial x$, ideoque $V = ws$; tum vero, posito $\partial w = w'\partial v$, ob $\partial v = \frac{x\partial x + y\partial y + z\partial z}{v}$ et $\partial s = \frac{p\partial p + q\partial q}{s}$, erit $\partial V = sw'\frac{(x\partial x + y\partial y + z\partial z)}{v} + \frac{w(p\partial p + q\partial q)}{s}$.
Hinc ergo habebimus: $M = \frac{w'sx}{v}$; $N = \frac{w'sy}{v}$; $N' = \frac{w'sz}{v}$; $P = \frac{wp}{s}$; $P' = \frac{wq}{s}$. Ex his porro colligitur:
$S = \frac{w(ss-pp-qq)}{s} = \frac{w}{s}$.
32. Ternae ergo aequationes, ex quibus solutionem peti oportet, erunt:
I. $\frac{w'sx\partial x}{s} = \partial\,.\,\frac{w}{s}$,
II. $\frac{w'sy\partial x}{v} = \partial\,.\,\frac{wp}{s}$,
III. $\frac{w'sz\partial x}{v} = \partial\,.\,\frac{wq}{s}$.
Hinc igitur cum sit: $\partial\,.\,\frac{wp}{s} = \frac{w\partial p}{s} + p\,.\,\partial\,.\,\frac{w}{s}$ et
$\partial\,.\,\frac{wq}{s} = \frac{w\partial q}{s} + q\,.\,\partial\,.\,\frac{w}{s}$,
si hic loco $\partial\,.\,\frac{w}{s}$ scribatur ejus valor ex I. aequatione $\frac{w'sx\partial x}{w}$, nanciscemur binas sequentes aequationes:
I. $\frac{w's}{v}(y\partial x - x\partial y) = \frac{w\partial p}{s}$,
II. $\frac{w's}{v}(z\partial x - x\partial z) = \frac{w\partial q}{s}$,
quae sub forma sequente repraesententur:
I. $\frac{y\partial x - x\partial y}{vv} = \frac{w\partial p}{w'vss}$ et
II. $\frac{z\partial x - x\partial z}{vv} = \frac{w\,\partial q}{w'vss}$,
haeque sunt binae aequationes, ex quibus solutionem desideratam derivare debemus.

items.quote: haeque sunt binae aequationes, ex quibus solutionem desideratam derivare debemus.
items.english: and these are the two equations from which we must derive the desired solution.
